think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 31-year-old woman presenting with destructive mucocutaneous ulcerations across the lower lip, gingiva, nasal septum, and back following multiple recurrences of cutaneous lesions, creating a diagnostic challenge between refractory tegumentary leishmaniasis, deep fungal mycoses (e.g., paracoccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis), and oral malignancy.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs in 2013 when the patient was admitted with submandibular lymphadenopathy and ulcerated lesions of the lower lip frenulum, gingiva, nasal septum, and back, prior to HIV serologic testing, repeat excisional biopsies, and fungal microbiological analysis.
3. Differential Distinctions: Deep fungal infections and oral malignancies present with identical destructive mucosal ulcerations and regional lymphadenopathy; however, excisional oral biopsy ruled out malignancy and microbiological fungal analysis was negative, while underlying HIV infection explained the atypical aggressive recurrence of Leishmania braziliensis.
case_prompt:
A 31-year-old Caucasian woman, currently unemployed, from Salvador, State of Bahia, Brazil, is admitted to the hospital with painful oral and nasal mucosal ulcerations, recurrent back lesions, and neck swelling. She has a two-year history of chronic, relapsing ulcerated skin lesions over her back that required repeated cycles of targeted antimicrobial therapy with only partial healing. Over the preceding weeks, she noted the appearance of new ulcerated lesions in the mouth and nose along with submandibular swelling.

On physical examination, the patient is in discomfort. Significant findings include tender submandibular lymphadenopathy and extensive ulcerated mucosal lesions involving the lower lip frenulum, the gingiva, and the nasal septum. A persistent ulcerated lesion is also noted over the dorsal back region. Baseline admission triage evaluation is performed.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Deep endemic mycoses are common causes of chronic mucosal ulcerations of the upper aerodigestive tract and regional lymphadenopathy in South America, but fungal cultures and microbiological investigations were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Microbiological analysis for fungi was negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Oral mucosal malignancy / Squamous cell carcinoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Chronic non-healing orofacial ulcers with regional lymphadenopathy in an adult strongly suggest neoplastic disease, but histopathologic evaluation of oral lesions failed to demonstrate neoplastic features.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Excisional biopsies of oral lesions were performed with unspecific result.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis with HIV co-infection
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The persistent and refractory mucosal ulcerations were driven by severe immunosuppression from undiagnosed HIV co-infection in a patient with biopsy-confirmed Leishmania braziliensis, which responded to antiretroviral therapy and liposomal amphotericin B.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Due to persistence of the lesions, HIV serology was performed. The patient was HIV positive and antiretroviral therapy was started (efavirenz 600mg, tenofovir 300mg, lamivudine 300mg, per day, one tablet containing the three drugs).

editor_comments: Admission narrative strictly stops before HIV testing, fungal analysis, and repeat biopsies. Look-alikes and pivot verified with exact article quotes.
